clues.subject: digital-literacy
clues.clue: Private string used to prove that an account belongs to you
clues.hint: Think of a secret sign-in detail you should never share.
clues.definition: A confidential sequence of characters used with an account name to verify a user's identity.
clues.signal: The clue points to a private sign-in credential that confirms account ownership during access.
clues.explanation: A password is the private string paired with an account name to demonstrate that the person signing in is authorized to use that account.

clues.subject: digital-literacy
clues.clue: Process that turns readable data into protected coded form
clues.hint: It keeps a message unreadable to people without the right key.
clues.definition: The conversion of readable information into coded data that requires an authorized method to restore it.
clues.signal: The wording contrasts ordinary readable data with a protected coded form that needs authorization to interpret.
clues.explanation: Encryption changes readable data into coded data so that only someone with the authorized key or method can restore and read the original information.

clues.subject: digital-literacy
clues.clue: App that retrieves and displays pages from the web
clues.hint: You use one to open sites, tabs, and online articles.
clues.definition: A software application that requests, interprets, and displays information from websites and other web resources.
clues.signal: Retrieving and displaying web pages describes the everyday job of a web-viewing application.
clues.explanation: A browser is the application that contacts web servers and renders their pages, allowing a person to read sites and move among online resources.

clues.subject: digital-literacy
clues.clue: Organized collection designed for storing and finding records
clues.hint: Think of a structured digital system for searchable information.
clues.definition: An organized collection of related data that can be stored, searched, updated, and managed electronically.
clues.signal: The terms organized, records, storing, and finding identify a structured system for managing related information.
clues.explanation: A database stores related records in an organized structure, making it practical to search for, update, and manage specific pieces of information.

clues.subject: digital-literacy
clues.clue: Clickable text or image that opens another online location
clues.hint: Selecting it can take you to a different page or section.
clues.definition: A selectable connection in digital content that leads a user to another document, page, file, or location.
clues.signal: The key signal is a selectable connection that transports a reader from one online location to another.
clues.explanation: A hyperlink is the selectable text or image that connects digital content to another destination, such as a page, file, or heading in a document.

clues.subject: digital-literacy
clues.clue: Programs and instructions that tell a device what to do
clues.hint: Unlike a keyboard or screen, this part of computing is not physical.
clues.definition: Programs, procedures, and related instructions that direct a computer or other digital device to perform tasks.
clues.signal: The clue describes nonphysical instructions that direct a device, distinguishing them from its tangible components.
clues.explanation: Software consists of programs and instructions that guide a digital device's actions, which is why the clue emphasizes telling a device what to do.

clues.subject: digital-literacy
clues.clue: Physical parts of a computer that you can touch
clues.hint: Think of tangible device pieces such as a monitor or mouse.
clues.definition: The physical, tangible components of a computer system and its connected devices.
clues.signal: The phrase physical parts that can be touched separates tangible equipment from programs and data.
clues.explanation: Hardware means the tangible parts of a computer system, so a monitor, mouse, processor, and cables fit the clue's focus on touchable components.

clues.subject: digital-literacy
clues.clue: Deceptive message that tries to steal personal account information
clues.hint: Treat unexpected requests for sign-in details with caution.
clues.definition: A fraudulent communication designed to trick people into revealing sensitive information or visiting an unsafe destination.
clues.signal: A deceptive message seeking personal account information is the central warning sign of this online scam.
clues.explanation: Phishing is a scam that uses deceptive messages to obtain sensitive information; the clue highlights the warning sign so students can avoid responding or clicking.

clues.subject: digital-literacy
clues.clue: Harmful program that can disrupt a device or expose data
clues.hint: Avoid unknown downloads and ask a trusted adult for help if concerned.
clues.definition: Software intentionally designed to damage, disrupt, spy on, or gain unauthorized access to a device or data.
clues.signal: The signal combines a harmful program with device disruption and exposed data, all common consequences of malicious software.
clues.explanation: Malware is software made to harm systems or compromise data. The clue names its possible effects to reinforce safe habits such as avoiding unknown downloads.

clues.subject: digital-literacy
clues.clue: Security barrier that filters network traffic using set rules
clues.hint: It helps a network allow trusted connections and block unwanted ones.
clues.definition: A hardware or software security control that monitors and filters network traffic according to defined rules.
clues.signal: Filtering network traffic by rules describes a protective boundary that decides which connections may pass.
clues.explanation: A firewall applies rules to network traffic, allowing permitted connections and blocking unwanted ones; this safety role is exactly the barrier described in the clue.

clues.subject: media-literacy
clues.clue: Person, publication, or place where information begins
clues.hint: Ask who created a claim before deciding whether to trust it.
clues.definition: The person, organization, document, publication, or location from which information originates.
clues.signal: The clue asks where information begins, directing attention to the origin behind a claim or report.
clues.explanation: A source is where information comes from, whether that is a person, publication, organization, or document; identifying it is the first step in evaluating a claim.
clues.requiredAttribution: Princeton WordNet used as a reference marker only.

clues.subject: media-literacy
clues.clue: Tendency that favors one viewpoint over fair balance
clues.hint: Look for uneven treatment of people, ideas, or evidence.
clues.definition: A preference or inclination that can shape how information, people, or viewpoints are selected and presented.
clues.signal: Favoring one viewpoint instead of providing fair balance points to a slant in selection or presentation.
clues.explanation: Bias is a tendency toward a particular viewpoint. The clue's focus on favoring one side explains why readers should notice what evidence or perspectives may be missing.
clues.requiredAttribution: Princeton WordNet used as a reference marker only.

clues.subject: media-literacy
clues.clue: Group a message is designed to reach or influence
clues.hint: Consider which people a creator expects will receive the message.
clues.definition: The intended group of readers, viewers, listeners, or users for whom a message is created.
clues.signal: Designed to reach or influence a group points to the people a creator expects to receive the message.
clues.explanation: An audience is the group a message targets. The clue emphasizes design and influence because creators often choose language, images, and platforms for those intended recipients.
clues.requiredAttribution: Princeton WordNet used as a reference marker only.

clues.subject: media-literacy
clues.clue: Choice of angle that guides how an issue is understood
clues.hint: Notice which details are emphasized and which are left outside the view.
clues.definition: The presentation of information through a selected angle, context, or emphasis that influences interpretation.
clues.signal: A chosen angle that guides understanding identifies the way presentation can shape interpretation without changing every fact.
clues.explanation: Framing is the selection of an angle, context, or emphasis for information. The clue describes how those choices guide an audience toward a particular understanding of an issue.

clues.subject: media-literacy
clues.clue: Material created to promote a cause through strategic influence
clues.hint: Examine whether strong emotional appeals support a larger cause or agenda.
clues.definition: Information or material used to promote a cause or viewpoint, often through selective or emotionally charged persuasion.
clues.signal: Promoting a cause through strategic influence signals organized persuasive material rather than neutral reporting.
clues.explanation: Propaganda is material designed to advance a cause or viewpoint. The clue emphasizes strategic influence because it may rely on selective information or emotional appeals to shape opinion.
clues.requiredAttribution: Princeton WordNet used as a reference marker only.

clues.subject: media-literacy
clues.clue: Quality of being believable because evidence and expertise support it
clues.hint: Check an author's qualifications, evidence, and track record.
clues.definition: The quality of being trusted or believed because a person, source, or claim appears reliable and well supported.
clues.signal: Believability supported by evidence and expertise describes the trustworthiness readers assess in a source or claim.
clues.explanation: Credibility is the quality that makes a source or claim worthy of belief. The clue links it to evidence and expertise because those features help readers judge reliability.
clues.requiredAttribution: Princeton WordNet used as a reference marker only.

clues.subject: media-literacy
clues.clue: Communication meant to move people toward a belief or action
clues.hint: Look for a message that tries to change what people think or do.
clues.definition: The act of influencing another person's beliefs, attitudes, decisions, or actions through communication.
clues.signal: Trying to move people toward a belief or action is the defining purpose of influential communication.
clues.explanation: Persuasion is communication intended to influence beliefs or actions. The clue directly describes that goal: moving an audience toward a chosen view or behavior.
clues.requiredAttribution: Princeton WordNet used as a reference marker only.

clues.subject: media-literacy
clues.clue: Short prominent title meant to summarize and attract readers
clues.hint: It usually appears above a news story and may shape first impressions.
clues.definition: A prominent title or caption that introduces a news story, article, or other item of media content.
clues.signal: A short, prominent title above a story is the usual label that gives readers their first impression of a news item.
clues.explanation: A headline is the prominent short title for a story. The clue mentions both summary and attraction because it signals the topic while also encouraging people to read further.
clues.requiredAttribution: Princeton WordNet used as a reference marker only.

clues.subject: media-literacy
clues.clue: Humorous imitation used to criticize people or social problems
clues.hint: Its jokes or exaggeration often carry a serious point underneath.
clues.definition: A form of expression that uses humor, irony, exaggeration, or imitation to criticize people, ideas, or society.
clues.signal: Humorous imitation paired with criticism identifies a genre that uses comedy and exaggeration to make a pointed observation.
clues.explanation: Satire uses humor, irony, or exaggeration to criticize a target. The clue connects imitation and social criticism because both are common techniques for delivering its underlying point.
clues.requiredAttribution: Princeton WordNet used as a reference marker only.

clues.subject: media-literacy
clues.clue: Paid message that promotes a product, service, or idea
clues.hint: It is created to encourage attention, interest, or a purchase.
clues.definition: A paid public message intended to promote or sell a product, service, organization, event, or idea.
clues.signal: A paid message that promotes something identifies commercial communication designed to attract attention or influence choices.
clues.explanation: An advertisement is a paid promotional message. The clue names products, services, and ideas because advertising can encourage interest or action across all of those categories.
clues.requiredAttribution: Princeton WordNet used as a reference marker only.
